sources: PreProcess.transform_ops in inference.yml at model revision b8f84f0b80c529de40b4fbb3544b84fa7233a513
note: ONNX model expects BGR. Source PNG is loaded in BGR channel order. No RGB conversion applied.
channelOrderEvidence: DecodeImage.img_mode: BGR, channel_first: false in inference.yml. cv2.imdecode returns BGR HWC directly, so no conversion step exists in this path at all.
branchSelectionEvidence: RecResizeImg.__call__ chooses resize_norm_img_chinese only when eval_mode is set, or when infer_mode is set with a character_dict_path. inference.yml sets neither infer_mode nor eval_mode, so the padding branch applies.
steps: resizedWidth = 320 if ceil(48 * ratio) > 320 else ceil(48 * ratio)

normalization.note: Upstream applies one scalar mean and one scalar standard deviation, not a per-channel [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] vector. Numerically identical, but recorded as implemented.

interpolation.reason: In the padding branch upstream calls cv2.resize without passing its `interpolation` argument, so the OpenCV default INTER_LINEAR applies. The argument is only threaded through the non-padding branch.
interpolation.pillowNotUsedForResizeReason: Pillow's BILINEAR filter is support-scaled and antialiases on downscale, so it would not reproduce cv2.INTER_LINEAR. Pillow is used only to render the synthetic sentinel.

padding.note: Padding is zeros in NORMALIZED space, which corresponds to mid-grey rather than black in pixel space. The tensor width is therefore always 320, not the resized width.

dynamicAxes.source: PIR graph input `x`; trt_dynamic_shapes in inference.yml lists [1,3,48,160], [1,3,48,320] and [8,3,48,3200]

recordedPerInvocation: source PNG sha256, width and height
transformed tensor shape, dtype and sha256 over the contiguous float32 buffer
honestDescription: The model does not receive unchanged pixels. It receives the synthetic PNG followed by the model's own required transform: BGR decode, aspect-preserving resize to height 48 capped at width 320, scaling to [-1, 1], and zero-padding to width 320. That transform is a property of the model, not a preprocessing choice made by this probe; the only choice made here was to reproduce it with the same resampler upstream uses.
